gaps.sentence: Teenagers ___ hours every day on social media.
gaps.hint: to use time or money on something (neutral)
gaps.explanation: 'Spend time/money on something' is the neutral verb for using time or money; 'waste' implies useless use.

gaps.sentence: The new timetable has ___ every commuter in the county.
gaps.explanation: 'Affect' = influence; 'effect' as a verb means bring about.

gaps.sentence: The ___ issue of the magazine has an interview with the president.
gaps.explanation: 'Current' means happening or existing now; 'actual' means real as opposed to possible or estimated.

gaps.sentence: He ___ on the sofa all afternoon yesterday.
gaps.explanation: 'Lay' is the past of 'lie' (recline): he lay on the sofa. 'Laid' would need an object.

gaps.sentence: Please be ___ — the baby is sleeping.
gaps.explanation: 'Quiet' means making little or no noise; 'quite' is an adverb meaning fairly or completely.

gaps.sentence: This smell ___ me of my childhood.
gaps.explanation: 'Remind somebody of something' means to make someone think of something; 'remember' is not followed by an object + of.

gaps.sentence: Unemployment has ___ sharply since the spring.
gaps.explanation: 'Has risen' — rise does not take an object.

gaps.sentence: Our team has a good ___ of winning on Saturday.
gaps.hint: pattern: have a good ___ of doing something
gaps.explanation: 'Have a chance of doing something' is the standard collocation for the likelihood of success.
